pattern: A replicated, partitioned append-only log: make writes sequential, make reader state a single offset, replicate each partition with a leader elected by a small consensus group, and bound disk by deleting whole segments. Ordering, scale and durability are all per partition.

tips.nudge: Who puts data into the system, and into what?
tips.hint: Write a functional requirement for sending messages to a named topic.
tips.show: F1: Producers publish messages (key, value, headers) to a named topic.

tips.nudge: Three different services want the same events. What do they each get?
tips.hint: Capture how applications read: each application sees everything, and its instances share the work.
tips.show: F3: Consumers subscribe as groups: each group receives every message; members of a group split the partitions.

tips.nudge: A broker's disk dies one second after it said 'got it'. What did you promise?
tips.hint: State what an acknowledgement guarantees and which failures it survives.
tips.show: N2: An acknowledged message survives the loss of any single broker or availability zone.

tips.nudge: 'Order created', then 'order paid'. Must every consumer see them in that order? And events of two different orders?
tips.hint: Say at what scope order is guaranteed.
tips.show: F2: Messages with the same key are delivered in the order they were produced (no global order).

checks.label: How long data stays, and why that matters

tips.nudge: A consumer shipped a bug yesterday. Can it read yesterday's messages again?
tips.hint: Add requirements for retention and replay.
tips.show: F4/F5: Consumers can rewind to an offset or time; topics keep 7 days by default, or the latest value per key (compaction).

tips.nudge: Write down the peak, not only the average.
tips.hint: Messages per second at peak and on average.
tips.show: peak_msgs = 1M /s; avg_msgs = 300k /s.

tips.nudge: Brokers run out of disk and network bandwidth before CPU. How many bytes per second?
tips.hint: messages/s × message size; then × replication factor for writes and × consumer groups for reads.
tips.show: ingress = 1M × 1 KB = 1 GB/s; replicated writes 3 GB/s; consumer egress ≈ 3 GB/s.

checks.label: Storage for the retention period estimated

tips.nudge: Seven days of everything, times how many copies?
tips.hint: average bytes/s × 7 days × replication factor.
tips.show: 300k/s × 1 KB × 7 days ≈ 180 TB raw, ≈ 540 TB with 3 replicas.

tips.nudge: Which runs out first on a broker: disk or network?
tips.hint: Divide replicated storage by usable disk per broker and compare with the network budget; add headroom.
tips.show: 540 TB / 20 TB ≈ 27 brokers for disk; with 50% headroom ≈ 40 brokers (network: ~5 GB/s total out / 40 ≈ 125 MB/s each, fine).

tips.nudge: What does a producer send, to whom, and what does it get back?
tips.hint: A batch of keyed records to the partition leader, with an acks setting; the answer tells where they landed.
tips.show: Produce(topic, [{key, value, headers}], acks, producer_id, sequence) → {partition, base_offset}

tips.nudge: A consumer asks for 'more'. More from where?
tips.hint: A read by partition and position, which can wait for new data.
tips.show: Fetch(topic, partition, offset, max_bytes, max_wait_ms) → record batches + high watermark

checks.label: How messages are laid out on disk modelled

tips.nudge: What is the cheapest structure to write to at 1 GB/s and read from any position?
tips.hint: Think files, appends and a position number.
tips.show: partition log: per topic-partition, segment files (base_offset.log) + sparse offset index; records [offset, ts, key, value].

tips.nudge: A consumer restarts. Where does it continue from?
tips.hint: Store one number per reader and partition.
tips.show: committed offsets: (group, topic, partition) → offset, kept in a compacted internal topic.

checks.label: The core storage structure designed as a part

tips.nudge: Before replication and consumers: how is one stream of messages stored and read fast?
tips.hint: Add a part for storage: compare database rows, an in-memory queue with acks, and a partitioned append-only log.
tips.show: Part 'Partitioned log': key hash → partition; each partition an append-only log of segments + offset index; sequential IO, page cache, zero-copy.

checks.label: Surviving broker loss designed as a part

tips.nudge: A broker dies. Who has its data, and who takes over writes?
tips.hint: Add a part for replication: compare async backup, sync-to-all, a quorum per partition, and leader + in-sync replicas with a controller.
tips.show: Part 'Replication': RF 3 across zones, followers pull, acks=all with min ISR 2, Raft controller elects leaders from the ISR with epochs.

checks.label: Sharing and tracking reads designed as a part

tips.nudge: Ten instances of one service read one topic. How do they split it, and how do they resume?
tips.hint: Add a part for consumption: compare broker-tracked per-message acks with consumer-pulled committed offsets and partition assignment.
tips.show: Part 'Consumer groups': consumers pull; one committed offset per (group, partition) in a compacted topic; a group coordinator assigns partitions.

checks.label: Bounding disk use designed as a part

tips.nudge: Nothing is deleted when it's read. So when is anything deleted?
tips.hint: Add a part for retention: compare delete-on-consume, per-message TTL, segment deletion, compaction and tiered storage.
tips.show: Part 'Retention': delete closed segments by time/size; compact keyed topics to the latest value per key; tier old segments to object storage.

checks.label: Cluster metadata has one source of truth

tips.nudge: Two brokers both think they lead partition 7. What prevents that?
tips.hint: Something strongly consistent must own leadership and membership.
tips.show: A controller quorum (KRaft/Raft, or ZooKeeper/etcd) stores metadata and elects partition leaders with epochs.

tips.nudge: Draw where the second and third copies of a message come from.
tips.hint: Connect the replica brokers to the leader and label the flow.
tips.show: Follower brokers → leader: 'fetch from offset (replicate)'.

tips.nudge: A consumer crashes after processing a message but before saving its position. What happens next?
tips.hint: Compare committing before vs after processing, and what it would take to get exactly-once.
tips.show: At-least-once by default + idempotent producer (producer_id + sequence); exactly-once via transactions that write outputs and offsets atomically.

tips.nudge: A broker holding 1,000 partition leaders loses power. Walk through the next 10 seconds.
tips.hint: Cover broker loss, zone loss, slow followers and consumer crashes.
tips.show: Controller elects new leaders from the ISR; producers retry idempotently; slow followers leave the ISR; a dead consumer's partitions are reassigned and resume from committed offsets.

tips.nudge: Traffic triples. What do you add, and what can't you change easily?
tips.hint: Think brokers, partitions (and the key remapping they cause), and retention.
tips.show: Add brokers and reassign partitions (throttled); add partitions knowing keys remap; tiered storage for longer retention; separate clusters per domain.
